title: C482/278/2020 of MAHMOOD Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Misc. Application No.278 of 2020
Mahmood ..... Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & another ....Respondents
Mr. Pankaj Kumar Sharma, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. S.S. Adhikari, AGA for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
This petition does not reveal as to which order is under
challenge. What is stated is that impugned orders be set aside.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that non
bailable warrants have been issued against the petitioner, as he could not
appear on the date of hearing due to the death in his family. Therefore,
time may be given to him so that he may appear before the court.
3. Fact may be looked into briefly. Charge sheet under
Sections 504 and 506 IPC was submitted against the petitioner, which is
the basis of Criminal Case No. 49 of 2020, State Vs. Mahmood, in the
Court of learned 2nd Additional Civil Judge/ Judicial Magistrate,
Roorkee (for short "the case"). The charge sheet was submitted on
01.03.2014. The case was fixed at the stage of evidence. But, when on
31.05.2018, the petitioner did not appear, the court directed issuance of
non bailable warrants against him. Since thereafter, the petitioner has
not been appearing in the case. Various dates have been fixed. Copy of
the order sheet, which has been submitted by the petitioner reveals that
on 20.01.2020, again, it was ordered that non bailable warrants and
notices to sureties be issued, fixing 13.02.2020. In para 7 of his
affidavit, petitioner states that on 07.11.2018, his two children died in a
road accident, therefore, he was in depression.

2
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the
record.
5. As stated, non bailable warrants were already issued
against the petitioner on 31.05.2018. What prevented him to appear on
31.05.2018 and thereafter? Moreover, warrants have been issued by the
court below why the petitioner has approached this Court is not
understandable. Petitioner would have appeared before the Court
concerned and assigned the reason for his non appearance. It is also true
that since 31.05.2018, non bailable warrants and process have been
issued against the petitioner, which has yet not been served upon him.
He comes before the Court to quash the non bailable warrants. Petitioner
needs no direction from the Court for his appearance, since non bailable
warrants have already been issued against him and he is free to appear
before the concerned court on any working days during court hours.
6. In the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of
the view that there is no substance in this petition. It is devoid of merit
and deserves to be dismissed.
7. The petition is dismissed accordingly.
(Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 14.02.2020
Jitendra
